text:
ConocoPhillips barely moved today, down just 0.07%, but it's up 5.34% over two weeks as crude oil prices have surged. The stock's recent gains reflect a sharp spike in global oil prices — the world price jumped to $125.44 per barrel — driven by escalating tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran-backed forces and Hurricane Isaias disrupting U.S. Gulf of Mexico production. These supply disruptions have tightened the fuel market at a time when refineries are already strained from damage caused by wars in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.

The modest decline today despite ongoing bullish news suggests the market may be pricing in some relief from a Trump-Putin diesel deal, which could ease refinery constraints and global fuel prices over time. However, the persistent geopolitical tensions and production risks keep underlying support for oil prices intact.
